subject: archaeology
intro: Archaeology leads to fieldwork and museums: contract archaeologists digging ahead of construction, specialists dating and analysing finds, and the curators and archivists who keep the past catalogued and public.

roles.title: Anthropologists and Archeologists
roles.what: Study past and present human societies: survey and excavate sites, recover and record tools, pottery and other material evidence, analyse finds in the lab, and write up the history, customs and living habits of earlier peoples.
roles.where: The whole field sequence is the job — survey and remote sensing, stratigraphic excavation and recording, dating methods, artefact and zooarchaeological analysis, and cultural resource management.

roles.title: Anthropology and Archeology Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach archaeology and anthropology at universities: lecture on theory and method, lead field schools and lab sessions, supervise student research, and publish the studies that keep the discipline moving.
roles.where: This course's Renfrew-and-Bahn arc — scope, survey, excavation, dating, interpretation and heritage ethics — is the standard intro curriculum such teachers deliver and research around.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Preserve records of permanent value: appraise documents, photographs and files, arrange and catalogue them to professional standards, find preservation solutions for fragile material, and help researchers find what they need.
roles.where: Unit 3's recording systems and context discipline, unit 7's looting and repatriation ethics, and unit 8's digital archaeology topics feed directly into archival appraisal and cataloguing work.

roles.title: Curators
roles.what: Build and run museum collections: acquire and authenticate artefacts, plan exhibitions and their interpretation, negotiate loans, manage budgets, and decide how a collection tells its story to the public.
roles.where: The heritage, ethics and management unit — cultural resource management, repatriation debates and public archaeology — plus artefact analysis from unit 5, is a curator's core training.

roles.title: Museum Technicians and Conservators
roles.what: Keep collections alive behind the scenes: catalogue and condition-check objects, clean and repair artefacts with conservation methods, prepare items for storage and transport, and install and maintain exhibitions.
roles.where: Unit 5's lithic and ceramic analysis and human-remains handling, and the dating and lab methods of unit 4, supply the object-handling and materials knowledge conservation work runs on.
